narrativeProgression.description: The man in the suit introduces himself as Ryan O'Donnell, a candidate for Ward 3 City Council, and expresses gratitude to the organizers and attendees of the forum.
O'Donnell mentions that he has been campaigning since April and has knocked on numerous doors, highlighting his active engagement with the community.
O'Donnell reflects on the rewarding nature of the campaign process and emphasizes the importance of understanding the issues affecting Ward 3 firsthand.

O'Donnell highlights the diverse nature of Ward 3, encompassing downtown, the Meadows, the Island, and South House and Kay Hill apartments, and emphasizes his commitment to representing all residents.
O'Donnell asserts that every resident of Ward 3 deserves good representation and that this is his primary goal in running for office.

O'Donnell expresses his belief in common ground among residents, including the desire for a responsive city government, sound investments in schools and infrastructure, and equitable distribution of resources.
O'Donnell acknowledges the existence of differing opinions and emphasizes the importance of a progressive tax code and equitable burden-sharing, advocating for middle-income families and the poor.
O'Donnell suggests that voters should choose a councilor who understands policy details, listens to all perspectives, and respects different viewpoints.
O'Donnell emphasizes his commitment to representing every part of Ward 3 and working collaboratively to achieve common goals.
O'Donnell concludes his speech by expressing his willingness to engage in further discussions after the forum.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Thank you very much.
My name is Ryan O'Donnell.
I'm running for Ward 3 City Council.
And like the other candidates, before me, I want to thank the Ward 3 Neighborhood Association
and Jerry Budger and everyone else who organized this.
And thanks to all of you for being here today.
I guess I'd start like this.
I started running in April.
And since that time, I've knocked on literally hundreds and hundreds of doors.
And some more than once.
And this process has been really enormously rewarding for me.
It's been an enriching educational experience ago and do this kind of, I have this kind of
conversation with so many people.
And I don't know any other way actually to get to know the issues that affect Ward 3 other
than doing that.
And I also think it's important because, as you know, Ward 3 is a tremendously diverse
ward.
We have downtown, we have the Meadows, we have all the way down to the island, we have
Salvo House and K-Hill apartments.
And what I'd like to say is that every single person in Ward 3 deserves good representation.
And that's my goal getting into this.
Also from these conversations, one thing that I have learned and really take the heart
is that there really is a tremendous amount that we all agree on despite these differences.
And for example, we all want a responsive city government.
We all believe in making sound investments in our schools in certain infrastructure like
our roads and that this investment ought to be made equitably throughout the city and
certainly in Ward 3.
I think many of us believe that in general the financial burden in our society ought not
to fall on those who can least afford it, middle-income families and the poor.
And I'm a supporter of progressive tax code at the state level and anything we can do
in that spirit here in the city of North Hampton.
Now there's going to be a lot of things as you've just heard that we don't agree on.
And when we come to issues like that, what I would suggest is important is you look for
a counselor who, number one, can get into the policy details of the issue at hand and
you can have confidence that he or she can do a good job navigating through that.
Two that you have a counselor who genuinely, genuinely wants to listen to all sides of
a debate and will listen to you and show you that respect even if we disagree on an issue.
And three, a counselor who's going to do the job and from time to time work on issues
for which there are no good solutions and make decisions that aren't pleasant to make.
So that's the kind of counselor I want to be.
I'm running for Ward 3 to represent every single part of the ward and I look forward
to the opportunity to work with everyone because I think that when we recognize what we
do agree on, we can come to a common sense of purpose about many things.
And I look forward to January when a new council convenes with a common sense of purpose.
I think when Ward 3 works together, we've shown that we can accomplish a great deal.
And I look forward to being part of that process with you.
I don't get any questions today, do I?
But I am here if you want to talk after this forum, I'm more than happy to do that.
Thank you.
